title: Sports: The Mindset of a Champion
coreMove: Talent opens doors in sport, but championship character is built by taking responsibility for preparation, feedback, team value, and recovery after losses.

exampleSpecs.stakes: the club may overpay for visible tools and ignore learning habits
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Billy Beane and Moneyball to question raw-tool worship

exampleSpecs.audience: players tempted to sulk or blame
exampleSpecs.stakes: a loss could become either practice material or identity damage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Michael Jordan to convert exclusion or defeat into practice design
use John McEnroe to separate winning talent from responsibility after losing

exampleSpecs.audience: athletes who feel discounted by visible traits
exampleSpecs.stakes: the runner may accept a narrow story about who belongs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Muhammad Ali, Larry Bird, and Wilma Rudolph to broaden athletic greatness beyond obvious early gifts

exampleSpecs.stakes: children may interpret bench time as fixed athletic rank
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Stuart Biddle youth sport research to show early beliefs shaping persistence

exampleSpecs.stakes: winning could hide weak team habits
